jobs.title: Community Outreach Facilitator at Polk County Conservation
jobs.description: Employer: Polk County Conservation Expires: 11/28/2026 The Community Outreach Facilitator plays a crucial role in supporting and expanding the Polk County Conservation Community unity Volunteer Program. This position works directly in the field alongside PCC staff and community volunteers, providing on-site guidance and support on community volunteer-assigned projects and at scheduled events that connect community volunteers with meaningful outdoor work. This role is highly field-focused, with an emphasis on being present with community volunteers in natural areas, helping them succeed in their assigned projects, and strengthening community involvement in conservation. One Three-Quarter Time Community Outreach Facilitator will serve with Polk County Conservation as part of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program. AmeriCorps volunteers develop skills that build a strong, leadership-packed résumé; earn a living stipend ($16,620) paid out equally over the course of 1200 hours of service; and receive a Segal Education Award upon completion ($5,176.50) to pay for higher education or qualified student loans. This position is a Three-Quarter Time volunteer, who will serve a minimum of 1200 hours over 39 weeks, serving 39 hours per week. This posting is not a direct position of Polk County Conservation, and successful applicants will not be employees of Polk County. Successful applicants will not be subject to terms and conditions of Polk County employment and will not be eligible for any employee benefits provided by Polk County. However, these positions will be serving with Polk County Conservation, a host site of the Polk County Conservation AmeriCorps Program, and will be subject to AmeriCorps rules, benefits, and federal requirements. Daily TimesThe typical weekly schedule will be established with the selected candidate to ensure they do not exceed 40 hours per week, candidates can expect the typical schedule to fall within Monday through Friday 6:30 AM to 4:30 PM Every service day will include two 15-minute breaks; additional breaks must be taken if the temperature is above 85 degreesA 30-minute lunch period is included with every service day; these 30 minutes cannot be counted towards the required service hours during the termHours during the week can be flexed to ensure the volunteer has a sustainable workload when a special evening or weekend event is scheduled during a given service week, volunteer will have access to event calendar a minimum of two weeks in advance of the scheduled event Volunteer will serve 1-2 Saturdays per month during their term; most Saturday events take place from 10 AM to 12 PM Volunteer is expected to show up before the start of an event to assist with setup and logistics and to stay after the end of the event to assist with cleanup and inventory of supplies Evenings and weekends are built into the schedule with a minimum of two weeks' notice prior to a volunteer being assigned Listed below are key annual events that occur during the spring, summer, and fall: May | Spring Into Action | Woodland Restoration June | National Trails Day | Trail Construction April, May, June | Tree Planting at identified priority woodland October | Moonlight Seed HarvestThe typical weekly schedule may change to better meet the needs of the Natural Resources Department* Volunteers must not serve any hours on the major federal holidays – New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. This includes checking emails, self-directed training, or teleservice. If the Host Site is open on one of these holidays and volunteers are expected to serve, the site supervisor should work with Program to gain approval for this volunteer service prior to the holiday. For any of the other federal holidays, including MLK Day, Presidents Day, Indigenous Peoples’ Day, and Veterans Day, Host Sites will communicate expectations of volunteer service in advance. If the Host Site is closed on one of more of those lesser holidays (including the day after Thanksgiving or Christmas eve) or the Host Site recognizes other workdays when major federal holidays fall on weekend days, volunteers should not check their email, complete timesheets, or do teleservice on those days either unless they follow the procedure above. Sick or personal leave, and holidays is allowed, but such time off does not count towards the required number of hours needed to successfully complete the term of service. There are additional benefits offered if the volunteer has a compelling personal circumstance. TrainingAll volunteers will go through two weeks of intensive in-person training to learn all the skills necessary to complete the volunteer duties outlined below.The Natural Resources Volunteer Outreach Representative AmeriCorps Volunteer will lead community volunteers and actively participate in a variety of natural resources management and conservation activities. The focus of the position is hands-on service, fostering environmental stewardship, and contributing to the overall improvement and preservation of natural habitats through the assistance of community volunteers. The Volunteer Outreach Representative will be responsible for leading community volunteers in executing impactful projects such as invasive species removal, prairie seed harvest, trail maintenance, garden bed maintenance, and tree planting. Failure to complete these trainings and certifications in a timely manner will result in a volunteer not receiving integral certifications utilized by the Program. Missing or skipping trainings and certifications could impact the ability of a volunteer to remain enrolled within the Program. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Graduate Internship - Research Library at Federal Reserve Board
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Board Expires: 11/30/2026 About the Division and Section/TeamThe Federal Reserve Board Research Library is offering two paid summer internships for graduate-level library or information science students to advance several projects that will improve library services for Board researchers. We offer a full array of customized library services to staff members throughout the Board, with particular focus on data-intensive research, data acquisitions and cataloging, research curation, metadata and taxonomy, automation development, and AI support.About the RoleTo enhance discoverability and use of the Board's data and research resources, projects will focus on data- and metadata-related initiatives that build on our recent system migrations, including the Federal Reserve Data Inventory and the Library Catalog Search. Interns will also collaborate with librarians and developers on strategies for using generative AI tools to streamline content integration across systems.Learning outcomes include practical experience in metadata cataloging, library system maintenance (including reporting and acquisitions data), process documentation, and research support—skills that transfer directly to positions in academic, research, and corporate libraries and information centers.Depending on the interns' skills and interests, they will work on at least two of the following projects:Metadata and Cataloging – Federal Reserve Data Inventory: To aid the roll-out and expansion of the Board's data inventory, interns will tackle metadata projects in line with national, international, and agency standards. This work may include: ongoing metadata curation, refinement and maintenance; and developing quality checks among systems. It supports the foundation and capability layers of the Board's enterprise-wide technology modernization work.Metadata and Cataloging – Library Services Platform (LSP): To aid the roll-out and expansion of our library catalog, interns will tackle metadata projects in line with national, international, and local standards. This work may include: ongoing metadata curation, refinement and maintenance; crafting draft records; and developing quality checks among systems.Technology, Software, and Process Improvements: To bolster workflow efficiencies, interns will conduct task analysis and workflow documentation to identify automation opportunities, document processes and code, and work with internal AI technology as appropriate.Taxonomies and Controlled Vocabularies: To enable discovery, interoperability, and process efficiencies in our catalogs and other discovery systems, interns will support the development and maintenance of taxonomy and authority control by working on the Federal Reserve Subject Taxonomy (FRST) and Federal Reserve Authority of Names (FRAN). jobs.title: Cabin Counselor at Camp Bear Creek
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 12/01/2026 Cabin Counselor – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Being a Cabin Counselor is exhausting. It’s messy. It’s challenging. And it’s also one of the most rewarding things you can do with your summer.Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.What We’re Looking For:We want people who:Love working with kidsCan serve as strong, positive role modelsAre ready to lead Are excited to help young people grow in faithDon’t mind unplugging and spending a summer in the woodsWe aren't going to lie, being a camp counselor is incredibly hard work. You’ll be responsible for the daily care and well-being of the campers in your cabin — making sure they eat, sleep, brush their teeth, wear socks, and feel safe. It looks different each week and could mean sitting up with them at night when they're scared of the dark. It means teaching them how to paddle a kayak, supporting them at the rock wall/zip lines, building fires for skillet enchiladas (you’re going to love it), dancing to Grooveship worship and answering their questions about Jesus in Bible It also means picking up a kid when they fall in the dirt, giving them a high five when they finally hit the bullseye in archery, and letting them cover you in mud in the creek. It's all part of walking alongside campers through a week of fun, growth, and faith—and helping give them a summer they'll never forget.At Camp Bear Creek, counselors don’t just supervise- they lead. You’ll gain real world experience in:Leadership and public speakingCurriculum planning and facilitationConflict resolution and creative problem-solving Teamwork across diverse backgrounds. These soft skills are essential in every career field. You’ll also lead a variety of camp activities and work with different age groups- giving you the opportunity to grow into a well-rounded leader. We are also willing to work with you to ensure that this job can be used for internship credit in fields like Education, Public Health, Recreation & Leisure, Youth Services, Psychology and more. However, any student in any field can benefit from a summer camp experience like this. You’ll be part of an incredible team of about 30 college-aged staff from across Iowa, the U.S., and even around the world. We work hard. We play hard. We show up for each other every day. You’ll be surrounded by people who push you to grow — and who feel like family by the end of week one. This is more than a job. It’s a ministry, a leadership opportunity, and a summer you’ll never forget. You’ll give this job everything you’ve got — and it will give even more back.So, if you're looking for a summer full of purpose, adventure, community, and growth, don't let this opportunity pass you by. For more information about working at Camp Bear Creek or to apply, visit https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/

jobs.title: Activity Counselor Summer Internship at Camp Merri-Mac for Girls
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Merri-Mac for Girls Expires: 12/02/2026 Cabin/Activity Counselor Camp Merri-Mac is a christian summer camp for girls ages 6 - 16. Located high up in the Blue Ridge mountains of North Carolina, girls come to camp for over 80 years to have fun. We believe the happiest environment is one in which the love of God is demonstrated by the staff and felt by all. We are often asked what makes camp so special. No one expects a simple answer, which is good, because there really isn’t one. The best we can come up with is that we pay attention to details, and we’re really good at building places where girls grow through friends and adventure. Merri-Mac is a traditional, family-run, Christian summer camp. Those buzz-words mean we offer a wide range of activities, we operate as an extended community that is close knit and family-oriented, and that we hire and maintain a Christian staff and environment. We are not a church camp or a sports camp and we love having children from lots of different backgrounds. We also carefully balance competition and cooperation as well as in-camp and out-of-camp activities. Merri-Mac counselors stand in positions of Christian leadership. As such each must demonstrate a serious Christian commitment, a high view of scripture and an abiding understanding of grace. We also hire camp counselors who are winsome and gentle in the way they care for children from different backgrounds. Cabin CounselorA cabin counselor lives in a cabin with their campers and 2-3 other staff, partially separated in a “counselor’s section” of the cabin. Each counselor will either lead or assist in an activity that matches their skills during the day. The main focus of a cabin counselor is to pour their lives into the lives of their campers; it is both hard and extremely rewarding work. See attached files for how to promote working at camp on your resume and a full length job description. This paid position is also offered as a summer internship! With over 240 hours of hands on teaching, lesson implementation and planning, and classroom management skills - it is a great boost to any resume!For more information on available positions this summer, contact our Associate Director, Andrea Young at andrea@merri-mac.com or 828-668-8766. Interested in a similar experience geared towards boys? Camp Timberlake for Boys is the answer! Check out our brother camp located just 20 miles over the mountain in Marion, North Carolina. Experience the same levels of growth through friends and adventure with their team!

jobs.title: Spring Outdoor Education Internship at Deer Hill Expeditions
jobs.description: Employer: Deer Hill Expeditions Expires: 12/03/2026 Spring Internship Dates: March 15 - May 30Ready to find your footing in the world of outdoor education? Deer Hill's internship program has been a core part of our wilderness expeditionary learning program for over 20 years, and has prepared countless young folks with the tools and skills necessary to get their start in the industry.As an intern at Deer Hill, your focus will be primarily on learning the foundations of expeditionary logistics - the "behind the scenes" work that makes our trips possible. Of course, the work can sometimes be demanding and unglamorous. However, in return you will be trusted with real responsibility, gain practical experience in the systems behind professional wilderness programs, and build deep connections with our guides, gaining mentorship and direct experience working alongside them.No previous outdoor-industry experience is required. We're looking for people who are dependable, curious, willing to learn, and excited to get their start in outdoor education. Whether you're studying outdoor education, interested in becoming a guide, or simply looking for a purposeful opportunity that you can feel passionate and proud of - we'd love to hear from you!What You Will Do:Pack food and equipment for wilderness expeditions Organize river, backpacking, and service-program gear Drive DHE vehicles and trailers throughout the Four Corners Support expedition launches, resupplies, and pickups Perform vehicle pre-trip inspections and troubleshoot problems in the field Clean, de-issue, maintain, and repair expedition equipment Outfit students with personal outdoor equipment Support Basecamp meals and kitchen operations Complete seasonal property maintenance and facility projects Assist with administrative projects and expedition documentation Support program preparation, transitions, and debriefs What You Will Learn:Wilderness expedition logistics and resupply systems Food, equipment, and inventory management Remote-area driving and trailer operations Vehicle preparation and field troubleshooting Equipment maintenance and repair Basecamp and program operations Planning and execution of wilderness education programs Life at Deer Hill:Interns live together in the Loft, our dedicated intern housing at Basecamp. The Loft is our newest and most modern staff housing, with six bedrooms, four bathrooms, a full kitchen, dining area, and common living space.Our 140-acre Basecamp is about 10 minutes from Mancos and 40 minutes from Durango. On days off, interns have access to DHE outdoor equipment and extensive local knowledge for exploring the Four Corners.Staff regularly find time for climbing, backpacking, paddling, running, hiking, and other adventures together, depending on programming and water levels.Community is a major part of life at Deer Hill. You'll live and work alongside a small group of people pursuing the same kind of work, and former interns consistently tell us that the relationships they build here are one of the best parts of the experience. Dates: March 15 - May 30, 2027These are our standard internship dates, and Interns should plan to be available for the full period. Some flexibility with start or end dates may be possible. Pleach reach out during the application process to discuss your availability.Spring is a busy programming season. Interns typically work 5-6 days a week. Most days begin with an 8:30 AM meeting and wrap up around 5:00 PM, although program logistics occasionally require earlier starts, longer days, or overnight field support. Qualifications:20 years of age minimum. Able to work legally in the United States. Valid driver’s license and clean driving record. Ability to pass criminal background checks. Able to carry 50 pounds. Be comfortable driving long distances and camping Be willing to learn new skills, including equipment repair Communicate effectively and work cooperatively with others Take initiative and follow through on responsibilities Benefits:$1,584 travel and living stipend. Housing provided for the duration of the internship Home-cooked meals when Basecamp groups are being fed Access to DHE food supplies and pantry when meals are not being providedFree personal use of DHE camping and outdoor equipment, subject to availability Access to Outdoor Prolink, NRS, and other professional gear-purchase programs Professional development opportunities throughout the season Potential opportunities for additional paid work after the internship

jobs.title: 2027 PAID SUMMER LEGAL INTERNSHIPS at Legal Services of the Hudson Valley
jobs.description: Employer: Legal Services of the Hudson Valley Expires: 12/04/2026 About Us For more than 50 years, Legal Services of the Hudson Valley (LSHV) has been providing free, high-quality legal counsel in civil matters when basic human needs are at stake, including eviction and foreclosure prevention, domestic violence, disability, elder law, healthcare, consumer fraud and more. Our services support almost 600,000 poor and low-income families and individuals who cannot afford an attorney in our seven-county service area. With the gap separating those who can and cannot afford legal representation widening each day, we work to ensure that everyone has equal access to justice, regardless of their ability to pay. As the only provider of comprehensive civil legal services in the lower and mid-Hudson Valley (Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess, Rockland, Orange, Ulster and Sullivan), LSHV is proud to have handled over 12,000 cases impacting over 27,000 household members including over 10,000 children last year. LSHV is made up of ten offices, and a dedicated and highly skilled staff of attorneys, paralegals, and administrative professionals. Legal Services of Hudson Valley is dedicated to building a highly skilled workforce that reflects the diverse communities we serve and where everyone feels supported to bring their authentic selves to work. We are committed to racial justice and promoting equity for all, and we continuously review and strengthen our processes and practices to support our staff, clients and the communities we serve. Respect is a cornerstone of relationships among our staff. Our employee resource groups are self-directed and provide a space for members to support one another and their shared vision. We encourage applications from people of all identities and backgrounds. Fellowship Description LSHV will host 10 law student fellows in our housing units and 10 law student fellows in our general and/or other practice area units. Through these fellowships, LSHV will train the next generation of social justice lawyers, giving them both practical litigation experience and an understanding of the factors that create disadvantages for low-income individuals and families. While helping LSHV attorneys and staff serve clients, law fellows will receive training, mentorship, support, and skill development and engage in advocacy. Work may include client interviewing, issue spotting, legal research and writing, preparing court documents, accompanying attorneys and clients to court, and appearing in court under a student practice order. Housing Unit Fellows will help our clients to maintain the basic human and legal right to live in habitable housing and lend support to LSHV’s efforts to challenge landlord intimidation and harassment. General Practice Fellows will assist our staff attorneys in a variety of practice areas, including family law and domestic violence, housing, veterans’ benefits, public benefits, consumer debt, disability, and/or immigration law. Details 10-weekfellowship duration; 35 hours per work week required (5-day week, Mon – Fri) $8,000 stipend with 5 days paid time off (PTO) Fellows will be placed in LSHV offices throughout our service area, including White Plains, Yonkers, Mount Vernon, Peekskill, Poughkeepsie, New Windsor, Goshen, Nanuet, Monticello, and Kingston. Fellows will be loaned laptops during the summer for conducting LSHV business. Housing, transportation, work-related, and other fellowship expenses will be the law student's responsibility. LSHV will provide office parking where applicable. At the conclusion of the summer, fellows may be required to provide feedback concerning their experience, the substance of which may be reproduced in full or in part in LSHV materials. Eligibility Open to law students enrolled in a U.S. law school who will have completed two years of law school by May 2027 or are graduating in 2027. Must not have previously accepted an LSHV Paid Summer Legal Fellowship (previously titled LSHV Paid Summer Legal Internship). Must be able to work several days per week in person in the office where placed (our offices are hybrid, subject to disability-related reasonable accommodations. Ability to travel to the office where placed and other locations, such as courts, as needed. Application Timeline All materials must be submitted by Monday, December 21, 2026, at 11:59 pm (ET) Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered. Applicants selected for interviews will be notified in early January 2027. Finalists will be notified in early February 2027. Required Submissions Applications will be evaluated based upon review of the following: Complete Online Application with preferred office locations and practice areas Unofficial Law School Transcript Current Resume One legal writing sample on any topic (5-page limit) Statement of Interest (typed, double-spaced) Describe your commitment to public interest law and/or direct legal services, and what you hope to gain from LSHV’s Summer Internship Program. Please explain why you are interested in the practice area(s) you have preference in your application. You may include information such as personal experience, prior jobs, volunteer experience or internships and what you learned from them, as well as future career plans and professional goals. (750-word max) Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please email us at accommodate@lshv.org or call 914-949-1305 This email is created exclusively to assist disabled job seekers whose disability prevents them from being able to apply online. Only messages left for this purpose will be returned.

jobs.title: AIER Economic Research Internship - Spring 2027 at American Institute for Economic Research
jobs.description: Employer: American Institute for Economic Research Expires: 12/05/2026 The OpportunityAIER’s Internships are unparalleled professional opportunities for undergraduates considering careers in economic research, academia, or the private sector. They provide college students and recent graduates the opportunity to work closely with staff on projects relating to their interests and AIER’s mission, including scholarly research, policy analysis, editorial writing, as well opportunities in other departments.Our interns have leveraged their experiences to launch careers at organizations like The World Bank, The Institute for Justice, Deloitte, Morgan Stanley, and IBM and many other research institutes and companies across the world. A significant number of our former interns now teach and research at well-respected universities across the country.ResearchAt the core of the AIER internship program is a self-developed research project, in which each intern develops their research interest into the foundation of an academic conference presentation and/or journal article, as well as how to communicate their results to the general public.While building out their project, interns are coached on how to develop research ideas, how to ask and justify interesting and important research questions, select an appropriate methodology, present their findings to scholars and peers, and receive critical feedback.At the end of their internship, each intern presents their final product to AIER staff and visiting scholars and is advised on how to develop their project further. They leave not only with a research product, but a new understanding what engaging in deep, careful, and detailed analysis of issues relevant to life and liberty of individuals – not just to academic discussion – entails.CurriculumA robust reading-and-discussion curriculum is the basis of the AIER internship. Interns are presented with selections of leading academic writing on Public Choice analysis, the history of the Great Enrichment, US Debt and monetary policy, and the importance of property rights, among other topics.In a series of seminar-style discussions led by AIER researchers, they develop their understanding of the ideas and principles behind the texts, and, build an intellectual toolkit to bring to bear on economic problems in their future professional and/or academic careers.WorkshopsThrough a series of workshops, interns learn and practice the essentials of academic and popular writing, various research methods, fundamental and advanced techniques in econometrics, economic analysis through AIER economic indicators and Bloomberg terminal data, blockchain technology and cryptocurrency trading, and more.The workshops are led by experts from AIER and related organizations and are generally conducted face-to-face, so individualized feedback and mentoring can be prioritized.CompensationAIER interns are paid Massachusetts minimum wage.Accommodations, Meals, and TravelHousing is provided in the AIER manor or cottages right on campus, close to the beautiful town of Great Barrington. AIER covers travel costs to and from campus.DatesSpring 2027: January 31st - April 9th. Applications due by December 4th, 2026.Summer 2027: May 30th - August 6th. Applications due by March 5th, 2027.Fall 2027: August 29th - November 5th. Applications due by June 11th, 2027. Note: AIER's fully funded Seminar Series in Classical Liberalism is an excellent way to demonstrate your interest in economics and connect with AIER! Many of our fellows and interns were seminar participants. Learn more at https://aier.org/seminar-series/.

jobs.title: NIH Office of NIH History and Stetten Museum (ONHM) - Postdoctoral Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/06/2026 You must apply through Zintellect at Zintellect - National Institutes of Health (NIH) - NIH Office of NIH History and Stetten Museum (ONHM) - Postdoctoral Fellowship - NIH-ONHM-2026-0001Exciting Fellowship Opportunity for Postdocs!Under its newly relaunched Stetten Scholars program, the Office of NIH History and Stetten Museum (ONHM) is seeking candidates for two opportunities to research significant aspects of the history of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and to learn about the history of biomedical research in the US from subject-matter experts in NIH’s Institutes, Centers, and Offices (ICOs). One of the opportunities can focus on any aspect of NIH history. The second, sponsored by NIH’s Office of Research on Women’s Health (ORWH) in celebration of ORWH’s 35th anniversary, must focus on research in women’s health. Applicants who propose topics focused on the history of research in women’s health will automatically be considered for both positions.Project DescriptionAs part of the submission, the applicant will propose a research project centered on a topic of historical importance related to NIH’s contributions to biomedical knowledge and practice. Scholars selected for this opportunity will receive mentorship from at least one biomedical researcher in a relevant NIH ICO as well as from ONHM’s professional historians. Project proposals should be designed to take full advantage of this unique dual-learning opportunity to combine historical research and an enhanced understanding of scientific inquiry to foster a deeper, richer appreciation of the NIH's impact on science, medicine, and society. To learn more about ONHM and its historical resources, visit https://history.nih.gov/ or email us at history@nih.gov.What will I be doing?As an ONHM Stetten Scholar, you will learn to:Understand and Articulate the Historical Significance of NIH Research:Scholars will enhance their ability to analyze and explain the historical importance of a specified area of research initiated, conducted, or overseen by NIH. Projects should include an examination of how NIH research has addressed public, scientific, or governmental concerns over time, in part by identifying new questions, changes, or challenges that emerged as a result of its findings.Effectively Communicate Scientific and Historical Concepts to a General Audience:Scholars will master clearly and effectively explaining core scientific, clinical, and/or technical aspects of historically important developments rooted at NIH, especially in addressing audiences without specialized knowledge. This skill includes addressing outcomes such as new and unresolved scientific and technical questions, surprising findings, social and ethical considerations, or major shifts in standards, metrics, methodologies, or expectations. The goal is to make complex historical and scientific insights accessible and engaging for non-specialists.Present Historically and Scientifically Sound Insights to STEM Audiences:Fellows will refine their ability to communicate significant, historically accurate insights about NIH research to sophisticated STEM audiences. Specifically, they will learn to present historical findings in a way that resonates with established professionals and advanced trainees in fields in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics by ensuring sound, compelling integration of historical context and scientific rigor. The goal is to make historical context and considerations clear, engaging, and accessible to subject-matter experts in related scientific and technical fields.Why should I apply?Under the guidance of mentors in both historical research and relevant biomedical specialties, you will have the opportunity to develop your research skills as an historian; engage with active scientific and clinical researchers; and gain direct exposure to advanced intellectual techniques, tools, and technologies. This opportunity provides a platform to work with scientific and clinical experts as well as professional historians; enhance your ability to connect with broader audiences regarding biomedical topics; and provide an educational, real-world experience that can enhance your career path.Visit ONHM’s website at https://history.nih.gov/ or email the staff at history@nih.gov to explore the historical resources related to your research interests.Where will I be located?Bethesda, MarylandWhat are the provisions?Participants will receive:A $71,000 stipend, paid monthly, as determined by the Office of NIH History & Stetten Museum.Health insurance supplemental allowanceReimbursement for training-related travel and conference attendance when program funding allows.What is the length of the appointment and potential start date?Appointments are for one year with potential renewal for one additional year.Start dates are flexible and coordinated with the selected candidate and mentors to ensure best outcomes. Selected fellows should plan to begin in the Summer of 2027.When are selections made?Selections will be made in April 2027. Nature of the AppointmentThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Participants do not become employees of NIH, ONHM, ORAU, ORISE, DOE, or any other agency, and there are no employment-related benefits. Instead, the participant will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment.While participants will not enter into an employment relationship, this opportunity will require a suitability/background investigation conducted by NIH. Any offer made is considered tentative, pending favorable outcome of the investigation.QualificationsTo be eligible, you must have earned your doctoral degree within five years of the appointment start date in one of the fields listed below. Your project proposal must demonstrate mastery of fundamental historical research methods and readiness for advanced training. Students who expect to complete their doctoral degree by the start date of the appointment are also encouraged to apply. Proof of completion must be provided before a selectee can start the position.U.S. citizens and U.S. Legal Permanent Residents (LPR) are eligible to apply. Applicants must be able to meet the security and access requirements of NIH. You must also be able to pass a federal background check. We strongly encourage you to carefully read the full terms and conditions. Ignoring this information could prevent you from taking part in the program.ApplicationsApplications must be submitted through the Zintellect application system no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard time on Monday, January 11, 2027. Incomplete applications will not be considered.All documents must be in English or include an official English translation.Supporting materials must be uploaded as PDF files to ensure the document can be searched by Zintellect’s search engine. All social security numbers, student identification numbers, and/or dates of birth must be removed (blanked out, blackened out, made illegible, etc.) before they are added to the application system.Materials not received via Zintellect (e.g., by email, postal mail, or fax) will not be considered.A complete application consists of:Complete Zintellect profileComplete Application questions Current Resume/CV, including academic history, employment history, and relevant experiencesTranscripts/Academic Records - Submit a copy of your most recent official transcript. For this opportunity, an unofficial transcript or copy of the student academic record printed by the applicant or by academic advisors from internal institution systems may be submitted to complete the application requirement, if you do not have a copy of your official transcript at the time of application. The transcript or academic record must include the name of the academic institution, name of the student, courses completed/in progress, grades and degree expected/awarded. A copy of your official transcript and/or letter showing proof of your degree may be required prior to starting the appointment. All transcripts must be in English or include an official English translation.Project proposal of no more than 1200 words, not including citations, with a clearly stated research question; a clear, central connection with the history of NIH; and demonstration of the standard skills required to conduct successful, historically sound research as well as the readiness and capacity to master more advanced skills with mentorship and training.Two (2) Academic or Professional Recommendations - Applicants are required to provide contact information for at least two recommenders in order to submit the application. Recommenders will be sent a notification from Zintellect. An application will not be considered complete unless at least two recommendations have been submitted through Zintellect before the application window closes. It is therefore suggested that you provide contact information for more than two recommenders to enhance your chances that your application will be complete before the deadline.If you have questions, send an email to NIHprograms@orau.org. Please include the reference code for this opportunity (NIH-ONHM-2026-0001) in the subject line or body of your email. Connect with ORISE...on the GO! Download the new ORISE GO mobile app in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to help you stay engaged, connected, and informed during your ORISE experience and beyond.

If needed, this selection date will be extended to January 8th. ----Cabrillo National Monument is seeking an enthusiastic, creative, and community-minded Community Volunteer Ambassador (CVA) to help strengthen one of the National Park Service's most innovative volunteer programs.This is far more than a traditional volunteer coordination internship. The CVA will help expand community partnerships, develop new volunteer recruitment strategies, improve volunteer experiences, and lead projects that create lasting impact throughout the park. Working alongside the Volunteer Coordinator, the CVA will collaborate with park staff across multiple divisions while gaining hands-on experience in volunteer management, community engagement, project management, partnership development, interpretation, and public service.The CVA will have the opportunity to develop and lead meaningful projects rather than simply assist with day-to-day operations. From coordinating volunteer events and improving onboarding experiences to building relationships with colleges, nonprofits, and community organizations, the CVA will help shape the future of Cabrillo National Monument's volunteer program.Professional development is a major focus of this position. The CVA will receive individualized mentorship, participate in career development opportunities, collaborate with staff throughout the park, and build skills that prepare them for careers with the National Park Service and other public service organizations.Previous Community Volunteer Ambassadors have gone on to permanent careers with the National Park Service, making this an exceptional opportunity for someone interested in conservation, public service, education, volunteer management, or community engagement.Skills You'll GainVolunteer ManagementCommunity OutreachPublic SpeakingPartnership DevelopmentEvent PlanningProject ManagementLeadershipProfessional CommunicationEnvironmental EducationInterpretationTeam CollaborationCommunity EngagementVolunteer RecruitmentProgram DevelopmentResponsibilitiesRecruit and engage new volunteers through community outreach and partnership development.Help coordinate volunteer recruitment events, including innovative "Volunteer Discovery Days" experiences.Build relationships with colleges, universities, nonprofit organizations, and community groups.Support implementation of Volunteer.gov and improve volunteer onboarding processes.Assist with volunteer orientation, training, and engagement initiatives.Help coordinate volunteer recognition events and professional development opportunities, including the Monumental Conference.Collaborate with park staff across multiple divisions on interdisciplinary projects.Develop educational materials, communication resources, and volunteer program documentation.Represent Cabrillo National Monument at outreach events, volunteer fairs, and community events.Assist with project planning, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the volunteer program.
